bug_description.normalized: The staged 77-byte witness is sent verbatim to libssh2's socketpair-based OSS-Fuzz client harness. A static parse of that stream shows the banner `SSH-\n`, then one SSH packet with `packet_length = 68`, `padding_length = 0`, and a 67-byte payload whose first byte is `SSH_MSG_KEXINIT` (20). In `_libssh2_packet_add()`, after skipping the packet-type byte and the 16-byte KEXINIT cookie, `_libssh2_get_string()` decodes the first name-list length as 46 and returns a haystack that is exactly the tail of the 67-byte payload: 15 spaces, one comma, and 30 spaces. `_libssh2_packet_add()` then calls `_libssh2_kex_agree_instr()` to search that list for the 28-byte needle `kex-strict-s-v00@openssh.com`. The start-of-list comparison fails, `memchr()` finds the only comma at offset 15, and `left = end_haystack - s` becomes 31 because it still counts the comma plus the 30-byte suffix. The vulnerable code increments `s` past the comma but forgets to decrement `left`, so the next loop iteration calls `memchr(s, ',', 31)` even though only 30 bytes remain. AddressSanitizer reports `heap-buffer-overflow` with `READ of size 31` in `_libssh2_kex_agree_instr` at `src/kex.c:3347`, and the staged fix closes the gap by adding `left--;` immediately after `s++` so the search bound tracks the advanced pointer.

source.description: The KEXINIT parser consumes attacker-controlled packet bytes and materializes the first algorithm name-list as `algs` plus `algs_len`, the exact haystack later scanned by `_libssh2_kex_agree_instr()`.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is 77 bytes. Interpreting bytes 5..76 as the SSH packet in the saved crashing path yields `packet_length = 68`, `payload_len = 67`, `msg = 20`, and a 32-bit name-list length of 46 at payload bytes 17..20. `_libssh2_get_string()` therefore returns `algs = data + 21` and `algs_len = 46`, and those 46 bytes are exactly `15 x 0x20`, `0x2c`, `30 x 0x20`, ending at the last byte of the 67-byte payload buffer.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

sink.code: while((s = (unsigned char *) memchr((char *) s, ',', left)) != NULL) {
sink.description: ASan sink. The second `memchr()` call searches 31 bytes from a pointer that has only 30 valid bytes left in the parsed name-list, so the read crosses the end of the packet buffer.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `READ of size 31` in `_libssh2_kex_agree_instr /src/libssh2/src/kex.c:3347:34` and states the invalid address is 0 bytes to the right of the 67-byte heap region allocated in `_libssh2_transport_read()`.

root_cause.description: After finding a comma, the code checks `left` while it still counts the comma byte, advances `s` past that comma, and leaves `left` unchanged. The remaining-byte bound becomes one byte too large for the suffix that the next `memchr()` scans.
root_cause.note: On the staged witness, `left` is 31 at the comma and `needle_len` is 28, so the guard passes. `s++` moves to a 30-byte suffix, but without the fix's `left--;` the stale value 31 survives into the next loop iteration.

tainted_value_origin.description: This parser call creates the tainted haystack and its length. On the staged witness it yields the 46-byte list whose only comma is at offset 15 and whose post-comma suffix is 30 bytes long.

parser_admitted.description: The saved crash stack shows `_libssh2_packet_add` running during initial key exchange, and static parsing of the staged payload gives `msg = 20` (`SSH_MSG_KEXINIT`). That dispatch enters the KEXINIT-specific parser that extracts the first algorithm list and calls `_libssh2_kex_agree_instr()`.

fine_trace.note: The crashing path is still in initial key exchange, and the statically parsed payload byte `msg = data[0]` is 20. That control decision selects the KEXINIT-specific branch that inspects the first name-list for the strict KEX token.

Source. The staged witness produces `datalen = 67`, so the `datalen < 17` rejection is not taken. After skipping the packet-type byte and 16-byte cookie, `_libssh2_get_string()` decodes bytes 17..20 as length 46 and returns `algs = data + 21`, `algs_len = 46`. Those 46 bytes are exactly 15 spaces, one comma, and 30 spaces, and they occupy the tail of the 67-byte payload buffer.

fine_trace.code:
if((strncmp((char *) haystack, (char *) needle, needle_len) == 0) &&
    (needle_len == haystack_len || haystack[needle_len] == ',')) {
fine_trace.note: The fast-path match at the start of the haystack does not return. The first 28 bytes of `algs` are spaces/comma/spaces rather than `kex-strict-s-v00@openssh.com`, so control falls through to the comma-search loop.

fine_trace.code:
while((s = (unsigned char *) memchr((char *) s, ',', left)) != NULL) {
        left = end_haystack - s;
fine_trace.note: With initial `s = haystack` and `left = haystack_len = 46`, `memchr()` finds the only comma at offset 15. Recomputing `left` from that comma yields 31 bytes from the comma through the end of the haystack, i.e. the comma plus the 30-byte suffix after it.

Root cause. The guard passes because `left == 31`, `haystack_len == 46`, and `needle_len == 28`. `s++` advances past the comma to a suffix of only 30 bytes, but `left` is not decremented, so the remaining-byte bound becomes one byte too large. The staged fix adds `left--;` at this point.

The post-comma token is 30 spaces, so the 28-byte comparison against the strict needle also fails. The function therefore does not return before the loop condition executes again with the stale `left = 31`.

fine_trace.code: while((s = (unsigned char *) memchr((char *) s, ',', left)) != NULL) {
fine_trace.note: Sink. The next `memchr()` uses `s = haystack + 16`, where only the 30-byte suffix remains, but `left` is still 31. ASan reports `READ of size 31` in this call and says the invalid address is 0 bytes to the right of the 67-byte heap region allocated in `_libssh2_transport_read()`.

allocation_context.note: ASan reports that the invalid read occurs 0 bytes to the right of a 67-byte heap region allocated here for the packet payload before `_libssh2_packet_add()` parses it.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The staged fix adds `left--;` immediately after `s++` in `_libssh2_kex_agree_instr()`. On the witnessed path that changes the second-loop bound from 31 to 30, matching the remaining suffix length and preventing `memchr()` from reading past the end of the haystack. Stage 02 did not execute the fixed image, so this is a source-level conclusion from the staged diff rather than fixed-runtime evidence.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: The trace derives `s` and `left` from the 46-byte name-list that occupies the tail of the same 67-byte packet buffer ASan reports from `_libssh2_transport_read()`, and the stale `left` at step 5 explains why the second `memchr()` crosses that allocation boundary.

poc.trigger: The staged 77-byte file `poc` is sent verbatim to the socketpair by `ssh2_client_fuzzer`. Stage 01's saved run reproduces `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow` with `READ of size 31` in `_libssh2_kex_agree_instr` at `src/kex.c:3347` and the stack `_libssh2_packet_add -> fullpacket -> _libssh2_transport_read`.

format.name: libssh2 ssh2_client_fuzzer raw socket stream
format.contract: Raw byte stream consumed as the server side of `libssh2_session_handshake()`. To preserve the witnessed path, the stream must match the staged KEXINIT layout at the source step: after the `SSH-\n` banner, the packet seen by `_libssh2_packet_add()` has `packet_length = 68`, payload byte 0 equal to `SSH_MSG_KEXINIT`, and its first name-list after the 16-byte cookie decodes to the exact 46-byte sequence `15 x 0x20, 0x2c, 30 x 0x20`. That makes `_libssh2_kex_agree_instr()` search a haystack of length 46, find the only comma at offset 15, and then reach the stale-bound case where `left` stays 31 while only 30 bytes remain.
